newsitem.title: USA: Crestar Financial, Citizens Bancorp to merge.
newsitem.headline: Crestar Financial, Citizens Bancorp to merge.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp. said Monday it has agreed to acquire Citizens Bancorp, a Laurel, Md.-based bank holding company with assets of $4.2 billion, in a deal valued at $774 million.
Citizens Bancorp stock jumped 45 percent, adding $14.50 to $46.75 in morning trade on the Nasdaq market. Crestar fell $2.625 to $58.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Citizens' shareholders will receive .835 share of Crestar common stock, or $51.25 per share, for each share of Citizens stock held.
The companies said the $774 million purchase price was based on Crestar's $61.375 per share closing price and 15.1 million Citizens' shares outstanding as of Friday, Sept. 13.
After the merger, Citizens will become part of Crestar.
Crestar, which operates 379 banking locations throughout Virginia, Washington, D.C. and Maryland, has total assets of $18.5 billion.

The transaction, which the companies expect to complete by March 31, 1997, will create an organisation with the largest deposit market share in the Greater Washington metropolitan area and the No. 2 position in the state of Maryland.

Richard Tilghman, chairman and chief executive officer of Crestar, said that one-time merger-related costs will hurt Crestar's results for the first quarter of 1997, but that the transaction will add to Crestar's earnings during the remainder of the year.

Crestar said that about 60 of Citizens' 103 branches are in markets where Crestar does not now operate. Most of the remaining branches are located near existing Crestar branches, so some consolidation can be expected, the company said.
The companies said stock buyback plans approved this summer by Crestar's and Citizens' boards of directors have been terminated effective immediately.
